open_points.subject: A21 state2_security_gate_pass
open_points.text:
state2_security_gate_pass
<-> every_required_category_has_one_outcome
    AND every_APPLICABLE_references_an_accepted_decision
    AND no_UNRESOLVED

Every reference resolves to an indexed item, and every APPLICABLE category
   references at least one indexed accepted decision of States 0–2.
open_points.question: Is resolution of every reference, including references beyond the one accepted decision required for an APPLICABLE category, a condition of state2_security_gate_pass, and must that condition be added to the formal invariant?
options: The formal invariant is exhaustive, so an APPLICABLE category passes when one reference is accepted even if another reference is unresolved.
The Required tests rule is also part of the gate, so every reference must resolve and the formal invariant is incomplete.
open_points.default_guess: Require every reference to resolve and add that predicate to the formal invariant.

witness.initial: A complete review has no UNRESOLVED categories; one APPLICABLE category has references A16 and Z99, where A16 is an indexed accepted decision and Z99 resolves to nothing.
events: The workbench evaluates the review before State 3.
outcomes: An implementation of the displayed biconditional passes because the category references an accepted decision.
An implementation of Required tests item 2 rejects because Z99 does not resolve to an indexed item.
witness.observer: The author attempting to proceed to State 3

open_points.subject: A21 review references
open_points.text: Every reference resolves to an indexed item
open_points.question: Which occurrences count as a reference: only identifiers in each `references:` field, or also identifiers in `affected:`, rationales, witnesses, and the surrounding review prose?
options: Only entries in the structured `references:` field.
Every identifier-like citation anywhere in the review record.
Entries in `references:` plus a specifically enumerated set of other fields.
open_points.default_guess: Treat only entries in the structured `references:` field as references and validate other fields under separately stated rules.

witness.initial: An APPLICABLE category has `references: A16` and `affected: M99`; A16 resolves, while M99 does not.
events: An author submits the otherwise complete review.
outcomes: A checker that treats only the `references:` field as references accepts the record.
A checker that treats `affected:` identifiers as references rejects the record.

open_points.subject: A21 indexed item resolution
open_points.question: Which index, item kinds, and state range define an `indexed item`, and how is an unqualified identifier resolved if more than one index can contain it?
options: The combined index of every named State 0–2 item, including K, M, and A items.
Only the accepted-decision index.
Any item in the repository-wide index, including later states.
A closed list of eligible item kinds stated by A21.
open_points.default_guess: Use the combined State 0–2 index, require globally unambiguous identifiers, and enumerate its eligible item kinds.

witness.initial: An APPLICABLE category has `references: A16, K-11`; A16 is an indexed accepted decision and K-11 is an indexed State 0 item but is not stored in the accepted-decision index.
outcomes: A resolver using the combined State 0–2 item index accepts both references.
A resolver using only the decision index rejects K-11.
witness.observer: The review author and the State 3 gate

open_points.subject: A21 APPLICABLE category evidence
open_points.text:
every APPLICABLE category
   references at least one indexed accepted decision of States 0–2
open_points.question: Must the accepted decision actually address the category and one of its affected boundaries, and if so, what recorded relationship proves that relevance?
options: Any indexed accepted decision of States 0–2 satisfies the rule.
The decision must name the category.
The decision must cover at least one boundary listed in the category's `affected:` field.
A separate category-to-decision relation must record the exact relied-on boundary.
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit category-to-decision relation identifying the boundary the decision covers.

witness.initial: The `secrets` category is APPLICABLE and references one indexed accepted decision whose subject and boundaries concern only concurrency.
events: The owner reviews the resulting security gate.
outcomes: A membership-only implementation accepts because the target is an indexed accepted decision.
A relevance-checking implementation rejects because the decision provides no secrets control.
witness.observer: The owner relying on the security review

open_points.subject: A21 self-reference
open_points.question: May A21 itself count as the accepted decision required by one of its own APPLICABLE categories, or must the qualifying decision be independently accepted before A21 is evaluated?
options: A21 may satisfy its own category because it is an accepted State 2 decision.
The current decision is excluded to prevent circular evidence.
A21 may be referenced only after a prior successful review record has accepted it.
open_points.default_guess: Exclude A21 itself from the decisions that can satisfy its gate.

witness.initial: A complete review has an APPLICABLE category whose only reference is A21.
events: The workbench evaluates A21 and its security review in the same State 2 closure.
outcomes: A resolver that treats the heading `Accepted decision A21` as already authoritative accepts the category.
A resolver that requires independent prior acceptance rejects the circular reference.

open_points.subject: A21 consequence
open_points.text: State 3 is blocked if any referenced decision is removed or loses its boundary.
open_points.question: What exact fact is a decision's `boundary`, which reference records reliance on it, and does losing any boundary, the category-relevant boundary, or all boundaries trigger the block?
options: Any change removing any boundary named by a referenced decision blocks State 3.
Only loss of the boundary relied on by this category blocks State 3.
Only loss of every boundary that made the decision relevant blocks State 3.
The decision-to-category reference must name the relied-on boundary explicitly.
open_points.default_guess: Make each category reference name the relied-on boundary and block only when that named boundary is removed.

witness.initial: An APPLICABLE category references an accepted decision that covers two boundaries, B1 and B2; the category relies on B1.
events: A later edit removes B2 but leaves B1 and the decision accepted and indexed.
The State 3 gate reevaluates the consequence.
outcomes: An implementation treating any boundary loss as sufficient blocks State 3.
An implementation tracking the category-relevant boundary allows State 3 because B1 remains.
witness.observer: The author attempting to enter State 3
